To the Aetna Medical Director:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of coverage for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG, CPT code 33533) for my 48-year-old patient, [Patient Name]. Please note that this letter is being submitted within the required 30-day appeal deadline. 

The denial letter indicates that coverage was denied under Aetna CPB 0286 because the submitted records allegedly lacked documentation of failed maximally tolerated medical therapy and did not include stress imaging within the prior 90 days to confirm high-risk anatomy. I respectfully request that this denial be overturned, as the planned surgical intervention is strictly medically necessary and delaying care poses an imminent threat to the patient’s life.

The patient suffers from atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris (ICD-10 I25.110). Regarding the requirement for recent stress imaging, performing a cardiac stress test on a patient actively experiencing unstable angina is an absolute clinical contraindication. Subjecting this patient to stress imaging would carry an unacceptably high risk of inducing a myocardial infarction or fatal arrhythmia. 

Because stress testing was contraindicated, we relied on definitive anatomical evaluation. In alignment with the diagnostic frameworks discussed in Aetna CPB 0119 regarding advanced coronary imaging, the patient underwent direct coronary angiography/computed tomography angiography. This recent imaging definitively documented critical, high-risk coronary anatomy—specifically, severe multi-vessel coronary artery disease that is not amenable to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The definitive anatomical evidence supersedes the need for functional stress testing, especially when such testing is medically dangerous.

Furthermore, the patient has already failed maximally tolerated medical therapy. Despite adherence to an optimal, guideline-directed pharmacological regimen (including beta-blockers, statins, and antiplatelet therapy), the patient continues to experience severe, refractory unstable angina. 

The clinical data clearly demonstrates that CABG is the most appropriate, medically necessary, and life-saving intervention for this patient. Denying this standard-of-care procedure based on the absence of a contraindicated stress test contradicts established cardiovascular guidelines. 

I have enclosed the patient’s complete medical records, including the recent coronary imaging reports that confirm high-risk anatomy, cardiology consultation notes, and a detailed medication history demonstrating the failure of medical therapy. 

Given the patient's highly unstable clinical condition, I respectfully request an expedited review of this appeal and an immediate authorization for CPT 33533. 

Sincerely,

[Physician Name], MD  
[Title/Specialty]  
[Practice Name]  
[Phone Number]  
[NPI Number]
